data_status: STRICT MODE: this dataset contains only values that were compared with, or ingested directly from, retrieved sources: JPL (SSD, SBDB), NASA (NSSDC fact sheets and mission catalog, Small Spacecraft SoA report 2026, SLS page, Apollo 11 press kit, NTRS papers, ), ULA, ESA, NIST, and the Launch Library 2 aggregator. Records carry source_authority/confidence where the source is an aggregator or vendor-reported compilation. Recalled, estimated and fictional values (optimizer catalog, costs, engine/vehicle specs without a retrievable source, the user-supplied SpaceX table) are not included. Derived values are computed only from verified inputs and are labelled derived.

record.spec_note: mass/power fields are taken from the first sentence in the NASA description that states a mass in kg or a power in W; they may describe a sub-unit or a mode. Read the sentence.
record.name: Accelerometer
record.description: The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft carried an accelerometer instrument designed to measure the change in velocity as the spacecraft performed aerobraking maneuvers in the martian thermosphere. The accelerometer data can be used to deduce atmospheric drag on the spacecraft, so atmospheric densities can be estimated. The z-axis accelerometer is aligned closely to the spacecraft velocity vector. It has a sensitivity of 0.332 mm/s per count, allowing measurements up to at least 170 km altitude. A typical set of accelerometer measurements during aerobraking spanned from about 200 s before periapsis to 200 s after periapsis, about 30 degrees of latitude. Additional measurements obtained before and after this period are used to determine accelerometer bias for each pass. Measurements are obtained every 0.1 s. Accelerations of 1 micro-g were detected.
